title: Launch planning for the new dashboard

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Hello, hello. Can you hear me all right?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Yes, we can hear you, Camille.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Hi Camille. Hi everyone.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Hi. Sorry, I'm in the office and it's a bit noisy, so I'll mute when I'm not talking.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: No problem, Thandiwe. Okay, the agenda's simple. We want to agree on a launch date for the new dashboard, what the launch looks like, and who does what. Lachlan, you sent a plan on Monday. Do you want to start?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Sure. So my proposal is a proper launch on Tuesday the seventeenth of November. A blog post, a short video Anouk's team is already working on, an email to every customer, and a webinar on the Thursday. And on the same day, we switch everyone to the new dashboard. One clean story. The old one's gone, here's the new one.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Everyone on the same day?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Everyone on the same day. Otherwise the message gets muddy.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Lachlan Whitcombe, I have to push back on that pretty hard. Lumière alone has about two hundred people using the old dashboard every morning. They built their own training around it, screenshots, a whole internal guide. If we switch them overnight, my phone won't stop ringing for a week.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: We'd warn them. That's what the email is for.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: An email two weeks before isn't a warning for a company that size. They need a month, minimum, and they need both versions side by side.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: But if we keep both, half of them will never move. That's exactly what happened with the old reports.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Can I say something?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Sorry, go ahead, Anouk.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Lachlan's not wrong about the old reports, Thandiwe. Nobody moved until we turned them off.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: That's true. But the old reports weren't the screen they open every single morning.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Okay. Before we decide that, Anouk, where are we on the design side? Is it actually ready for the seventeenth?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Mostly. There are two things I'm not happy with. The colors on the charts don't have enough contrast for people with low vision, and you still can't move through the filters with only the keyboard. Rafferty says both are about a week of work. I'd really rather not launch to everyone with those still open.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Can't those come in a follow-up?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: We could, but Lumière has an accessibility requirement in their contract. Thandiwe would know better than me.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: They do. It gets checked every year.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Okay, I didn't know that.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: And Tessellate? They've been on the beta for two months. Thandiwe, how are they finding it?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Tessellate loves it, honestly. Their operations lead told me it saves her team about an hour a day. They've asked me twice when the export to spreadsheets is coming.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Sorry, Thandiwe, you cut out for a second. An hour a day?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: An hour a day, yes. Their words, not mine.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Rafferty finished the export last week. It's already in the beta.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Oh, great. I'll tell them today.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: See, that's exactly the kind of story I want for the launch. Tessellate saving an hour a day, with a quote from them.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: I agree, that's a great story. Let me propose something, and you tell me what's wrong with it. We keep the seventeenth for the announcement, Lachlan. The blog, the video, the webinar, all of it. But the switch happens in two steps. From the seventeenth, the new dashboard is the default for everyone, with a link back to the old one for six weeks. Then we turn the old one off for good.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Six weeks is a long time. Four?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Six. Lumière freezes everything over the holidays, they won't train anyone in late December.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Fine, six. But the link back should be small. I don't want it to look like we're not sure about the new one.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: I can make it visible without shouting. A quiet line at the bottom of the page.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: And Anouk, the contrast and keyboard fixes have to be in before the seventeenth. Can you and Rafferty make that?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: If Rafferty starts on Monday, yes. I'll talk to Rafferty Quinlan this afternoon and confirm by tomorrow.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Thank you. Thandiwe, can you take Lumière personally? I'd like them to see it before the announcement, not find out from an email.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Yes. I'll offer them a training session the week before, on site if they want. I'll call their team lead on Friday.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: And Thandiwe, could you ask Tessellate for a quote? Two or three sentences is plenty.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: I'll ask today, along with the export news.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Great. I'll update the launch plan with the two steps and send it around by Wednesday. And I'll rewrite the email so it doesn't say the old one is gone.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Oh, and can I put the date in this week's newsletter, or is that too early?

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: The date is safe now. Go ahead, Lachlan.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Good. Lachlan, the webinar. Who's presenting?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: I was hoping you would, Camille, just five minutes at the start. Then Anouk Verhoeven shows the new design, and Thandiwe Mahlangu takes the questions.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Me taking the questions sounds dangerous.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: You know the customers best. That's exactly why.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: I'm happy to present, as long as nobody asks me to dance.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: No dancing, Anouk. Not this time.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Okay, I'll do the opening. Let me recap so we're all clear. The announcement stays on Tuesday the seventeenth of November, with the blog and the video, and the webinar on the Thursday. The new dashboard becomes the default that day, with a quiet link back to the old one for six weeks. Anouk and Rafferty finish the contrast and keyboard fixes before the launch, and Anouk confirms tomorrow. Thandiwe trains Lumière the week before and asks Tessellate for a quote. Lachlan sends the new plan by Wednesday. Did I forget anything?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: The video. I'll send you a first cut next Monday, Lachlan.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Perfect.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Nothing else from me, Camille.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Great. Thanks, everyone, that was quick.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Thanks, Camille. Bye.
